extracted.subtask_description: Critical guidance and evaluative observations about epic poetry (exemplified by commentary on Milton's Paradise Lost), plus related essays on education, conduct, and public prayer. The page offers principles for what makes poetic episodes, allegory, description, and schooling effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present the project's seed early
rubrics_metrics.description: Include, in the opening book, the Project upon which the whole Poem turns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reader may observe how just it was not to omit in the First Book the Project upon which the whole Poem turns: As also that the Prince of the fallen Angels was the only proper Person to give it Birth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the proper speaker for central proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign the proposal or driving idea of the poem to the character most fitted by rank and interest to originate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As also that the Prince of the fallen Angels was the only proper Person to give it Birth, and that the next to him in Dignity was the fittest to second and support it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prophetic/antecedent reports to dignify subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ ancient prophecy or report about a subject's pre-existence to elevate its dignity before it exists in the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is besides, I think, something wonderfully Beautiful, and very apt to affect the Readers Imagination in this ancient Prophecy or Report in Heaven, concerning the Creation of Man... Nothing could shew more the Dignity of the Species, than this Tradition which ran of them before their Existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe assemblies in a sublime, poetical manner
rubrics_metrics.description: When depicting large gatherings of great beings, aim for sublimity and elevated poetic tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rising of this great Assembly is described in a very Sublime and Poetical Manner. 'Their rising all at once was as the Sound / Of Thunder heard remote--'

rubrics_metrics.name: Make diversions suited to characters' nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the diversions, contests, and entertainments of characters to fit their capacities and moral condition (e.g., fallen angels whose strength and knowledge are misapplied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Diversions of the fallen Angels, with the particular Account of their Place of Habitation, are described with great Pregnancy of Thought... Such are their Contentions at the Race, and in Feats of Arms...

rubrics_metrics.name: Use music and discourse to reveal character and theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Let music and dialogue in the poem reflect the characters' preoccupations and themes (e.g., celebrating criminal exploits, debating fate, free-will, foreknowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their Musick is employed in celebrating their own criminal Exploits, and their Discourse in sounding the unfathomable Depths of Fate, Free-will and Fore-knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concise, suggestive lines to long descriptions for horror
rubrics_metrics.description: A single well-chosen line can convey monstrous horror more effectively than extended description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monstrous Animals produced in that Infernal World are represented by a single Line, which gives us a more horrid Idea of them, than a much longer Description would have done. '--Nature breeds, / Perverse, all monstrous, all prodigious Things...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use episodes to relieve main debate but avoid weakening the fable
rubrics_metrics.description: Include episodic descriptive passages to unbend the reader from central debates, but avoid spinning them out so long that they weaken the principal narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Episode of the fallen Spirits, and their Place of Habitation, comes in very happily to unbend the Mind of the Reader from its Attention to the Debate. An ordinary Poet would indeed have spun out so many Circumstances to a great Length, and by that means have weakned, instead of illustrated, the principal Fable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat sustained allegory with care within an epic
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegory can be a 'very finished Piece in its kind' but may be problematic when considered strictly as a part of an epic poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I have already declared my Opinion of the Allegory concerning Sin and Death, which is however a very finished Piece in its kind, when it is not considered as a Part of an Epic Poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct genealogies and symbolic relations with justness
rubrics_metrics.description: Design allegorical genealogies and relationships so that they arise naturally from plot events and appear logically consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Genealogy of the several Persons is contrived with great Delicacy. Sin is the Daughter of Satan, and Death the Offspring of Sin... I need not mention the Justness of Thought which is observed in the Generation of these several Symbolical Persons; that Sin was produced upon the first Revolt of Satan, that Death appear'd soon after he was cast into Hell...

rubrics_metrics.name: Personify abstractions vividly and nobly
rubrics_metrics.description: When personifying abstract concepts (e.g., Death, Sin), make the description strong, noble, and fitting to their symbolic weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The descriptive Part of this Allegory is likewise very strong, and full of Sublime Ideas. The Figure of Death, [the Regal Crown upon his Head,] his Menace of Satan, his advancing to the Combat, the Outcry at his Birth, are Circumstances too noble to be past over in Silence...

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance imaginative invention with probable, credible detail
rubrics_metrics.description: While fanciful personification and invention have a place, passages that include probable, physically imaginable incidents increase believability and reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Satan's Voyage through the Chaos there are several Imaginary Persons described... but for my own Part, I am pleased most with those Passages in this Description which carry in them a greater Measure of Probability, and are such as might possibly have happened. Of this kind is his first mounting in the Smoke... his falling into a Cloud of Nitre...

rubrics_metrics.name: Use striking imagery for key scene transitions (e.g., gates opening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Powerful, sensory imagery (sound, motion, light) should be used to mark crucial scene shifts to convey the poet's spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: '--On a sudden open fly / With impetuous Recoil and jarring Sound / Th' infernal Doors... Harsh Thunder, that the lowest Bottom shook / Of Erebus. She open'd, but to shut / Excell'd her Powr; the Gates wide open stood... So wide they stood, and like a Furnace Mouth / Cast forth redounding Smoak and ruddy Flame.' The Description of the Gates is very poetical, as the opening of them is full of Milton's Spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize moral development over mere worldly polish in education
rubrics_metrics.description: When choosing education methods consider that private education more readily fosters virtue and good-breeding, whereas public schooling tends toward worldly knowledge and assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A private Education promises in the first place Virtue and Good-Breeding; a publick School Manly Assurance, and an early Knowledge in the Ways of the World. Mr. Locke... is altogether for a private Education... That Virtue is much more difficult to be attained than Knowledge of the World; and that Vice is a more stubborn, as well as a more dangerous Fault than Sheepishness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value emulation and contests for developing liveliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Education in groups (public schools) supplies emulation, contention, and lively passions that train practical abilities (caution, secrecy, circumspection) useful in public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be objected... unless it be a Conversation with such as are in some measure their Equals in Parts and Years, there can be no room for Emulation, Contention, and several of the most lively Passions of the Mind... the well laying and carrying on of a design to rob an Orchard, trains up a Youth insensibly to Caution, Secrecy and Circumspection, and fits him for Matters of greater Importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure capable masters and adequate assistants in public schools
rubrics_metrics.description: A public school is only as good as the quality of its headmasters and their assistants; without sufficient care and encouragement, promising youth may be spoiled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It must however be confessed, that a Person at the head of a publick School has sometimes so many Boys under his Direction, that it is impossible he should extend a due proportion of his Care to each of them. This is, however, in reality, the Fault of the Age... In our great Schools indeed this Fault has been of late Years rectified, so that we have at present not only Ingenious Men for the chief Masters, but such as have proper Ushers and Assistants under them; I must nevertheless own, that for want of the same Encouragement in the Country, we have many a promising Genius spoiled and abused in those Seminaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize lasting social benefits of school friendships
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendships formed at school can provide long-term advantages and mutual assistance throughout life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quintilian... That we very often contract such Friendships at School, as are a Service to us all the following Part of our Lives. (Example story of Westminster friends rescuing one another.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid worldly epithets and inappropriate address in public prayers
rubrics_metrics.description: Clergy should refrain from applying worldly titles (Illustrious, Right, Reverend, Right Honourable) and parenthetical domestic asides in prayers, using the Liturgy as a pattern instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is it not Contradiction to say, Illustrious, Right, Reverend, and Right Honourable poor Sinners? These Distinctions are suited only to our State here, and have no place in Heaven: We see they are omitted in the Liturgy; which I think the Clergy should take for their Pattern in their own Forms of Devotion... 'Bless, as I am in Duty bound to pray, the right honourable the Countess; is not that as much as to say, Bless her, for thou knowest I am her Chaplain?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform talebearing by gentle correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Gossiping and talebearing in retired persons is an indecency that should be corrected tactfully, since it disturbs neighborhood peace; a respected friend or authority may reform them by setting the failing 'in a proper Light.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding this Frailty, the honest Gentleman is so happy as to have no Enemy: At the same time he has not one Friend who will venture to acquaint him with his Weakness. It is not to be doubted but if this Failing were set in a proper Light, he would quickly perceive the Indecency and evil Consequences of it.
